offers_products.reason: Offers financial products (leases, BNPL, cash advances), not manufactured goods or software licences; leased merchandise is incidental.

offers_services.reason: Provides consumer financial services: lease-to-own financing, Buy Now Pay Later, cash advances and payroll-deduction purchase programs.

sells_to_consumers.reason: Progressive Leasing, Four and MoneyApp serve individual consumers acquiring merchandise or cash advances.

sells_to_organizations.reason: Retailers partner with Progressive and Four; Purchasing Power sells to employers including Fortune 500s and government agencies.

recurring_revenue.reason: Revenue is mostly lease payments on individual transactions with short terms; customers often buy out early, so it is not subscription-like.

cyclical_demand.reason: Lease-to-own and cash advances serve credit-constrained consumers, whose demand often holds or rises in downturns.

big_ticket.reason: Lease payments and BNPL installments are small and frequent, though underlying goods like furniture and electronics cost more.

people_delivered.reason: Revenue comes from lease and financing platform and capital, not staff time; technology-based instant decisioning drives it.

large_customers.reason: Main customers are individual consumers using lease-to-own, BNPL and cash advances; retailers and employers are secondary.

asset_heavy.reason: Fintech lease-to-own and BNPL run on a tech platform; lease merchandise is bought from retailers and funded, not plants or fleets.

notes: Progressive Leasing is the largest part; the recurring_revenue answer is a judgment call because lease-to-own terms are short.
